title: It was better than I ever possibly could’ve imagined #ImmersivePhanto...
transcript: Now that I've had a full day to process what the heck I just saw, here are my full, non spoiler thoughts on masquerade. I've really never experienced anything quite like this because it really did feel like living in the world of a musical and going on a journey with these characters. It is essentially a walkthrough, guided experience. I know there were rumors that potentially some parts of the show could be a little bit more free roam, but that is definitely not the case. Between scenes, you are ushered around, being told exactly where to go, and when you get into a new room, being told exactly where to sit or stand. And while that may sound incredibly intrusive, strangely, it never took me out of the experience. They do such a good job keeping you engaged throughout, I was just always so excited to see what was around the next corner or what was in the next room. Even during these transitional periods, the world still feels alive and you still feel completely immersed. And I think that's one of the biggest accomplishments that they've pulled off here. And of course, it being Phantom of the opera, you expect spectacle, and they definitely deliver there. You do, of course, have a chandelier rising and falling, and it is magical both times, as well as other illusions and spectacle along the way that I won't dare spoil. But every single dollar, every single cent that you Spent on that ticket, you are going to see in this experience, they did not cut corners. They truly went all out in every single facet of this thing. Then, of course, you have the performers themselves, many of whom have been on Broadway, some of them in Phantom of the opera. And it is such a talented cast. It really does feel like being immersed in a Broadway show and watching these Broadway caliber talents in these highly themed environments perform from literally feet away, often interacting directly with you. It's just one of those experiences you cannot get anywhere else. I've mentioned character interactions, and I do want to clarify. You are never going to be pulled off into a room alone with a character, which is something that sleep no more and life and trust were really well known for. But there are many moments in the show that I won't spoil, but a character might come up to you and ask you a question, or maybe they hand you a prop. It all just makes you feel like you are a part of this world. You're not just an observer. Now, as for the actual story itself, there are deviations from the Phantom of the opera musical. All of the well known songs from the show are still here, as well as the major character beats. And it's just enough that if you are a fan of the material, you're going to see everything that you Wanted to see, but there's also a ton of it new mixed in that I think it's really gonna appeal to both old and new fans because everyone is going to have moments of awe and wonder and surprise. And I will say, coming out of the experience I immediately wanted to go back and do it again. Even though it will be functionally the same experience, there was still so much to take in that I think a second viewing will be beneficial. And being able to see a brand new cast put their own spin on it I think also will be really cool. There's so many other things I wanna say, but they are spoiler so I'll probably make a separate spoiler video. But if you were considering buying a ticket and were on the fence, let this be your sign. Go see the show. Bite the bullet. You will not regret it.
classificationReason: References 'masquerade' as title of immersive Phantom experience, but unclear if this is the actual off-Broadway Masquerade show from the list
